dialogue.text: [wry, storytelling] Level six is ten million dollars, and this client never comes to the branch. Mr. Pruitt grabs his coat and drives out to her.
Ten million doesn't take a number.

[wry, storytelling] He even brings pastries. She wants a beach house, but her money is in stocks, and selling them would mean a big tax bill. So she doesn't sell. The bank lends her the cash and holds on to her stocks, and if she ever can't pay, it just sells them. For a bank, that's about as safe as a loan gets.

[wry, storytelling] An hour later, Pruitt calls and has Jess print the loan papers. Jess's own credit card charges her about twenty-two percent a year. The woman with ten million pays less than half of that.
So the less you need the money, the cheaper it gets?
Now you're learning. At ten million, you're a house call.
